subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should strict plugin owner equality immediately make every legacy ownerless session unpatchable by plugin runtimes, or must OpenClaw provide a one-time ownership migration or recovery path first?
rationale: Failing closed prevents arbitrary plugin adoption, but it intentionally changes authority over persisted state created before ownership metadata existed; repository policy treats that compatibility and security boundary as maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed now
options.body: Accept operator or non-plugin recovery for ownerless rows, document the upgrade impact, and require deployed proof before merge.

options.title: Migrate legacy ownership
options.body: Add a narrow doctor or migration path that establishes legitimate ownership before strict runtime enforcement.

recommendation.title: Fail closed now
recommendation.body: Accept operator or non-plugin recovery for ownerless rows, document the upgrade impact, and require deployed proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most directly connects this contributor to the persisted session lifecycle and mutation machinery affected by the upgrade decision.
